title: unexpected-autoscaler-lease-decommit-during-replicaset-rotation
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Summary: During a regional replicaset rotation triggered by our control-plane deploy, the autoscaler erroneously decommitted active lease tokens from several reserved pools. This led to a gradual, hard-to-detect reduction in usable GPU capacity for affected dedicated tenants and intermittent elevated tail latency for burst traffic. Multiple customers experienced degraded throughput and elevated 429s over a 3 hour window before mitigations were applied.

What happened (brief): The autoscaler decision path evaluated warmup and lease accounting in the wrong ordering after a topology-change event. When the replicaset rotated, a race caused some lease holders to be marked 'orphaned' and their burst credits to be reconciled as spent, triggering the allocator to shrink effective headroom. The system then initiated conservative scale-down actions while tenant requests were still arriving, causing sustained shortfall.

Impact: High for a small number (~8) of mid-size dedicated tenants using burst concurrently in us-west-2. Symptoms included sustained 3x increase in p95 and transient 429s and queueing. No data exfiltration or privilege escalation.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2025-02-12 02:07 UTC: Control-plane rolling update started in us-west-2.
- 2025-02-12 02:12 UTC: First signs of elevated queue latency on dedicated route dashboards.
- 2025-02-12 02:27 UTC: Multiple on-call alerts and customer Slack escalations.
- 2025-02-12 03:05 UTC: Hotpatch (autoscaler conservative-disable) deployed to prevent further lease decommits.
- 2025-02-12 03:40 UTC: Fallback routing engaged for most affected tenants; 95th latency trends returned toward baseline.
- 2025-02-14 18:00 UTC: Root-cause identified in allocator lease-reconciliation and topology-change handling.
- 2025-02-25 10:30 UTC: Patch rolled forward in canary then global; monitoring confirms restored steady-state.

Root cause (technical): A regression introduced in the lease-accounting refactor changed the reconciliation semantics during replica handoff. Specifically: when a replica signals readiness transition, the reconciler performed final lease amortization prior to transferring live lease tokens. Under concurrent request load and a partially-applied topology update, some leases were double-counted as released and subsequently reconciled away from the reserved pool headroom. The autoscaler interpreted the lower headroom as safe to downscale and executed scale-down actions (including returning idle-GPU reservations), which exacerbated the capacity shortfall.

Mitigations applied:
- Immediate: Deployed a temporary guard that blocks any lease decommit while a replicaset rotation is in progress and marks leases as 'protect' until reconciliation window completes. This prevented further drops.
- Short-term: Enabled fallback routing to less-impacted pools and raised burst-credit thresholds for affected tenants to avoid spurious throttles.
- Long-term: Rewrote the reconciler transition ordering, added a two-phase lease transfer handshake, and added a conservative safety buffer to autoscaler headroom calculations.

Monitoring/alerts added:
- New alert (autoscaler.lease_decommit_rate) triggers at 5/min with runbook link.
- Dashboard tiles for live headroom vs. allocated leases and an anomaly detector for unexpected headroom drift.
- Synthetic workload to replay replicaset rotation under controlled load to catch regressions pre-merge.

Customer comms: Official status and postmortem shared with affected accounts and CSMs on 2025-02-18. Outbound notes included root cause, timeline, mitigations, and credits applied for impacted windows.

Action items (completed and follow-ups):
- Hotfix shipped and reverted autoscaler to conservative mode during rotations (Done).
- PR: runtime#4382 implements two-phase lease handoff and reconciliation ordering (Done).
- Add unit/integration tests for replicaset rotation scenarios (Done).
- Create end-to-end chaos test for lease handoff under load (In Progress, owner: S. Kim).
- Update runbook with exact steps to disable autoscaler decisions during topology changes (Done).
- Post-release follow-up: monitor for 14 days and confirm no recurrence (Completed).

Links: Confluence incident doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/incident/ENG-999782; Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4382; Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123456/p1676212345678900; Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/alloc-headroom/alloc-headroom-overview
